title: Third-party HSM control matrix and evidence handoff
summary: Working draft: mapping of customer security questionnaire items to Redwood and vendor evidence for third-party HSM/KMS usage in Dedicated/Private deployments. Includes workshop notes, evidence index, outstanding questions, and recommended next steps for POC handoff.
body:
Purpose: capture the answers and direct evidence we will present to customers who ask about hardware-backed key management (HSMs) used in Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private. This doc is scoped to the 3rd-party HSM model (Cloud HSM provided by vendor X) and how Redwood integrates with it for key wrapping, export controls, backups, and audit logging.

Context and audience: Solutions engineering and infosec reviewers at customer during POC/sales cycle. This is not a final compliance pack — it is a focused evidence handoff for HSM-specific controls.

Workshop summary (2026-02-10):
- Attendees: Leah (security), Arjun (infra eng), Marta (solutions eng), customer security lead (C), cloud vendor rep (V).
- Goal: validate that keys are generated in HSM, that Redwood cannot export plaintext model keys, and that audit logs show key usage tied to request IDs.
- Outcome: demoed key creation flow, KMS API calls, and K/V usage. Customer requested cryptographic proof (key attestations, CSR). Vendor will provide attestation bundle V-attestation-2026-02-09.zip.

Key points of integration (technical):
- Key lifecycle: keys are generated inside vendor HSM (non-exportable flag set). Redwood stores only armored references (key IDs) in our secrets store. Actual cryptographic operations (wrap/unwrap) are proxied to HSM via authenticated service account.
- Backup/restore: vendor supports sealed backup blobs that are encrypted with HSM-root master — vendor backup metadata files provided. Redwood maintains operational runbook for restoring wrapped keys into the same vendor HSM cluster with customer authorizations.
- Access control: HSM calls use mTLS and short-lived service tokens. Operator access requires audited MFA and is restricted to on-call SREs and the vendor's operations team when contracted.
- Audit trail: vendor HSM produces an append-only tamper-evident audit log. Redwood correlates KMS request IDs to application trace IDs and stores correlation metadata in our observability logs for 90 days by default (extendable for enterprise).

Evidence index (files to attach to customer packet or link to vendor portal):
- vendor-attestation-V-2026-02-09.zip
- kms-config-export-2026-02-15.pdf (sanitized config showing policy flags: non-exportable=true, origin=HSM)
- key-usage-trace-extract-2026-02-10.csv (sample of KMS request id -> Redwood request id mapping)
- mTLS-cert-chain-2026-02-08.pem (public certs used for mutual TLS between Redwood and vendor)
- operator-access-audit-2025-12-20.log (redacted operator session log - shows MFA steps)
- backup-manifest-vendor-2026-01-30.json (manifest of sealed backups)
- runbook-hsm-restore-POC-v1.docx (procedural steps for restore during tested POC flows)
- pen-test-summary-2025-Q4.pdf (relevant sections where cryptographic operations were validated)

Control mapping (selected customer questionnaire excerpts mapped to evidence):
- Q: Are keys generated and stored in hardware-backed modules?
  A -> Evidence: kms-config-export-2026-02-15.pdf; vendor-attestation-V-2026-02-09.zip

- Q: Can Redwood export plaintext keys or key material?
  A -> Evidence: kms-config-export-2026-02-15.pdf; runbook-hsm-restore-POC-v1.docx (describes only sealed backups; no plaintext export allowed).

- Q: How is operator access to keys controlled and logged?
  A -> Evidence: operator-access-audit-2025-12-20.log; mTLS-cert-chain-2026-02-08.pem; key-usage-trace-extract-2026-02-10.csv

- Q: Are there mechanisms for attestation/firmware verification of the HSM appliance?
  A -> Evidence: vendor-attestation-V-2026-02-09.zip; linked vendor hw-firmware-checksum-URL in linked_artifacts

- Q: Data residency and key locality during failover?
  A -> Evidence: backup-manifest-vendor-2026-01-30.json; runbook-hsm-restore-POC-v1.docx (describes that sealed backups are region-bound unless customer allows cross-region replication).

Open questions and risks (items to resolve before enterprise signoff):
- Attestation freshness: customer requests an attestation signed within 30 days of the contract signature. Action: request new attestation from vendor (owner: Vendor rep).
- Backup custody model: customer wants dual-control for restore. Current model: Redwood can initiate restore under customer approval, vendor must be engaged for some operations. Action: propose a signed runbook annex with explicit approval flow (owner: Leah).
- Log retention: customer requires 1 year of KMS call logs. Current default 90 days. Action: estimate storage + cost and produce pricing appendix (owner: Arjun).
- Hardware firmware verification cadence: customer wants cron-signed firmware manifests. Coordinate with vendor on cadence and proof-of-rescan APIs (owner: Marta).

Redwood-provided statements (draft language customer-facing):
- "Key material is generated inside the vendor HSM and marked non-exportable by policy; Redwood holds no plaintext key material for customer encryption keys."
- "All KMS calls from Redwood to the vendor are performed over mutual TLS with short-lived credentials and are logged with request identifiers that we correlate to application telemetry."
- "Backups use vendor-sealed blobs; restores require customer authorization plus operator steps logged and auditable."

Privacy & compliance notes:
- We treat cryptographic keys as sensitive metadata — any document showing key IDs or trace IDs must be redacted to remove specific key fingerprints before sharing with external parties. Evidence files in the index above have been sanitized; originals are stored in the compliance vault (link in linked_artifacts).

Next steps (high-priority for POC handoff):
- Attach vendor attestation with fresh signature (target 2026-02-24) [owner: Vendor rep].
- Produce pricing appendix for extended log retention and dual-control restore model (target 2026-02-21) [owner: Arjun].
- Draft runbook annex for dual-control restore and escalate for legal review (target 2026-02-23) [owner: Leah].
- Prepare a short slide deck (3 slides) summarizing attestation, non-exportability, and operator controls for the customer security review call (target 2026-02-20) [owner: Marta].

Notes to reviewers: this is intended as a working packet for POC security reviewers. Do not attach any unredacted private key material. If you need full logs for a customer audit, route a formal evidence request via security@redwood.com and we will push artifacts from the compliance vault under an NDA.
control_mapping: KMS-GEN: keys generated in HSM -> kms-config-export-2026-02-15.pdf, vendor-attestation-V-2026-02-09.zip

ATTESTATION: firmware and device attestation -> vendor-attestation-V-2026-02-09.zip
